Calendar

The syllabus is a living document and is liable to change. You will never get more reading than is listed here; readings may be swapped for something of equivalent length or less. There should be no more than ~30 pages of reading per class session, or around 1–1.5 hours of reading.

Readings hosted on libproxy.mit.edu require you to be signed in with your MIT certificates or Touchstone. Bring hard copies of the readings to class — you will need them for reading responses and discussion. Registrar deadlines and holidays are marked in the week where they fall.

Week 1

Introduction

Sep 9
What is media?
  • No assigned reading
  • ASSIGNED Syllabus quiz next class
Sep 11
Theories of media
  • IN CLASS AI declaration. Choose your track (support tool or conscientious objector) and say how you would be interested in using AI (if applicable).
  • IN CLASS Syllabus quiz

Fri Sep 11 — Registration deadline ($50 late fee).

Week 2

Information infrastructure

Sep 16
Books and print culture
  • Ann Blair, “Introduction” and “Epilogue” in Too Much to Know (2010)
    • How did people in early modern Europe collect and search for information?
    • What is the history of “information overload?”
  • ASSIGNED A1 “Create a dataset”
Sep 18
Libraries, archives, and information retrieval
  • Retrieval augmented generation, library classification schema, historical memory
Week 3

Images and evidence

Sep 23
Maps, charts, and abstraction
  • Catherine D’Ignazio and Lauren Klein, “Who Collects the Data? A Tale of Three Maps,” MIT SERC case studies (2021)
    • How are the three maps depicted in this case study similar?
    • How are they different?
  • ASSIGNED A3.1 project pitches
Sep 25
Images and the view from nowhere
  • Photography, objectivity, data visualization
  • In class A1 Protocol pre-registration
Week 4

Networks

Sep 30
Broadcast telecommunications
  • Gitelman and Mullaney, “Nineteenth-Century Media Technologies,” Information: A Historical Companion (2021)
    • How did the telegraph change the relationship between communication and transportation?
    • Do media technologies simply represent reality, or do they help construct it?
Oct 2
The physical internet
  • Data centers, internet cables, and global networks
  • The Digital Silk Road and Facebook’s Free Basics
  • Assigned A3.1 presentation date
Week 5

Project proposals

Oct 7
Project proposals, day 1
  • DUE A3.1 project pitches (link to deck TBD)
Oct 9
Project proposals, day 2
  • DUE A3.1 (continued)
  • Introduction to qualitative methods

Fri Oct 9 — Add Date. Last day to add full-term subjects.

Week 6

Political economy of new media

Oct 14
The data economy
  • Janet Vertesi, “Data Free Disney,” Public Books (2023)
    • Is privacy possible?
    • What tradeoffs are you willing or unwilling to make for digital services?
  • In class Draft project proposal
Oct 16
The attention economy
  • Quantifying and monetizing attention
  • AdSense and the economic foundations of the internet
  • Due A1 Create a dataset (9 am, submit on Canvas)
Week 7

Online communities

Oct 21
The creator economy
  • Angèle Christin and Yingdan Lu, “The Influencer Pay Gap: Platform Labor Meets Racial Capitalism,” New Media & Society (2023)
    • Who gets paid what for the same work, and how would you know?
    • What does it take to make a pay gap visible when everyone’s rate is private?
Oct 23
Fandoms and forums
  • Design and governance of fan fiction
  • K-pop fandoms and political advocacy
  • DueA3.2 Project proposal and annotated bibliography (9 am, submit on Canvas)
Week 8

Platform governance

Oct 28
Content moderation
  • Li and Zhou, “When content moderation is not about content: How Chinese social media platforms moderate content and why it matters,” New Media and Society (2024)
    • What are the benefits and risks of “ambient” content moderation?
    • Should platforms moderate a video differently based on the comments around it? Why?
Oct 30
Regulating content
  • FCC regulation, deregulation, and Section 230
  • Vertical integration

Research progress meetings open Oct 28. Sign up for a 30-minute slot between Oct 28 and Nov 6 (link TBD).

Week 9

Media industries

Nov 4
Journalism and the press
  • Professional norms of “objectivity” and muckraking
  • The local news crisis
  • Assigned A3.5 Oral peer review presentation date.
Nov 6
Public media
  • Ethan Zuckerman, “The Case for Digital Public Infrastructure” (2020)
    • What problem is digital public infrastructure trying to solve?
    • What challenges could make digital public infrastructure difficult to create or maintain?
  • Due A3.3 Last day for meetings
Week 10

Oral peer reviews

Nov 11
NO CLASS Veterans Day
Nov 13
Oral peer reviews, part 1
  • Due A3.4 First draft of final paper
  • Due A3.5 Oral peer review (draft of video or PechaKucha). Verbal critiques.

Midterm oral exams run Nov 9–17. Sign up for a 30-minute slot; your one-page handout is due online 24 hours before your slot.

Week 11

Peer reviews (cont'd) and internet culture

Nov 18
Oral peer reviews, part 2
  • Due A3.5 Oral peer review (cont’d)
Nov 20
Memes and virality
  • Matilde Catanese, “The year is a dropdown menu: Platformed provenance and the viral afterlives of AI-generated retro music,” New Media and Society (2026)
    • What role might debunking play in the future?
    • What evidence did listeners use to prove that this was an authentic “lost” recording?

Wed Nov 18 — Drop Date. Last day to cancel full-term subjects.

Week 12

Advertising and moral panics

Nov 25
Advertising and moral panics
  • The mechanics of Black Friday
  • Comics, violent video games, and addictive technology
Nov 27
NO CLASS Thanksgiving holiday
Week 13

Future of media, and final presentations begin

Dec 2
The labor behind artificial intelligence
  • Suresh et al., “Participation in the age of foundation models,” ACM FAccT (2024)
  • In class Assign presentation days
  • Due A3.5 Peer review memos (9 am, submit on Canvas)
Dec 4
Final presentations, day 1
  • Due A3.7 Personal review
  • Due A3.8 Final presentation paper (9 am, submit to Canvas)
  • Due A3.9 Final presentations begin
Week 14

Wrap up

Dec 9
Final presentations, day 2
  • In class Class memes (deck link TBD)
  • due A3.9 Final presentation
